releases.body:
**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Changed

- **Live search reads Kilo's current store, including LanceDB.** Kilo defaults to
  LanceDB now; `indexing_search` used to look only at Qdrant, so a healthy Kilo
  LanceDB answered as if Kilo had no index. Both stores are searched read-only,
  the project's `indexing.vectorStore` decides which one is active, and a stale
  index left behind by a store switch is not mixed into the results.
- **Kilo's project config is read with Kilo's own precedence.** Workspace and
  ancestor `kilo.jsonc`/`kilo.json`, `.kilo`/`.kilocode` directories, `KILO_CONFIG`,
  `KILO_CONFIG_DIR` and `KILO_CONFIG_CONTENT` can change the store, the LanceDB
  directory, the Qdrant URL and the embedding profile used to read Kilo. The own
  index keeps its own configuration and is not redirected by project scope.
- **A linked worktree is searched as baseline + delta, not just imported that
  way.** Delta hits win; a baseline hit is returned only when the file in this
  checkout still hashes to the value Kilo indexed in the main checkout. The
  lookup expands the limit when the hash filter removes too many hits, like
  Kilo's overlay.
- **`indexing_import` imports the same worktree pair as a build.** It uses the
  delta-first/baseline-skip plan, seeds the manifest so the next refresh does not
  re-embed what it copied, and reports the precise provider/schema/profile
  refusal instead of a generic incompatible-profile error.
- **Embedding models can be described without a code change.** `indexing.json`
  gained a `models` map (`dimension`, `queryPrefix`, `maxInputTokens`,
  `maxBatchItems`, `maxBatchTokens`, `scoreThreshold`) and the settings commands
  gained `dimension`, `queryprefix`, `maxinputtokens` and `modelscorethreshold`.
  A custom entry that changes a mirrored Kilo model warns that its index may no
  longer be importable.

### Added

- **Custom model metadata is editable from the Desktop settings page** through
  the native dimensions row, and the server's catalog now lists custom entries.
- **A weekly Kilo drift check.** `npm run check:kilo-mirror` compares the mirrored
  model registry and constants against Kilo upstream; the `kilo-drift` workflow
  runs it on a schedule and opens or closes one issue. It is not part of normal
  PR CI and never blocks on the network.
- **The README and bundled skill document live LanceDB search, project config,
  worktree search, custom models and the drift monitor.**

### Dependencies

- `@lancedb/lancedb` 0.41.0 (still reads databases written by Kilo 0.26.2) and
  OpenTUI 0.9.7. `mini-semantic-search` stays on 0.1.0 because 0.2 bundles a
  different 256d model, and OpenTUI pins Solid 1.x and web-tree-sitter 0.25.10.

**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Changed

- **An import says why a Kilo source is incompatible.** The profile comparison
  still decides it, but the report now names the reason — a provider this plugin
  has no adapter for (`kilo`, `bedrock`, `vercel-ai-gateway`), a
  provider/model/dimension mismatch, or a metadata schema it does not read —
  instead of leaving a bare `compatible: false` to be interpreted.
- **Kilo's LanceDB is read from every candidate directory.** Kilo 7.8.32
  defaults to LanceDB under its state directory, so the import looks for
  `<basename>-<hash16>` databases under `~/.local/state/kilo/indexing/lancedb`,
  the `XDG_STATE_HOME` and Windows equivalents, and the `opencode`-named
  directory older builds used; `KILO_INDEX_KILO_LANCEDB_DIR` still names the
  base explicitly. A missing candidate is not an error, and an unreadable one
  keeps its reason.
- **A linked worktree imports its baseline and its delta.** Kilo keeps the main
  worktree's database plus a delta for the linked one and merges them at search
  time; the import reads both and says which side is missing when only one
  exists, instead of reporting that there is no Kilo index. A workspace opened
  in a subdirectory of the worktree is mirrored into the main checkout the way
  Kilo mirrors it. Baseline files are re-hashed by the scan that follows, so a
  local change Kilo had not indexed yet is not mistaken for the main checkout's
  content.

### Added

- **The README documents Kilo's two source shapes, the importable providers and
  the worktree model**, and distinguishes Kilo's `semantic_search` from
  `indexing_search`. The bundled skill carries the same distinction, and a
  catalog test pins `kilo`, `bedrock` and `vercel-ai-gateway` as deliberately
  unsupported.

**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Changed
- **Index runs overlap network work and stop rewriting the manifest per batch.**
  Embedding and upsert batches now run concurrently (three in flight for hosted
  providers, one for the local model, overridable with
  `KILO_INDEX_EMBEDDING_CONCURRENCY`), manifest saves are coalesced, and path
  deletes are sent to the store in bounded batches. LanceDB reuses one
  connection per database through a per-database queue, search caches its
  metadata and auto-refresh checks, query embeddings run in parallel, and an
  imported manifest seeds file size and mtime with a bounded parallel `stat`
  pass.

### Added
- **`npm run perf` measures indexing throughput on synthetic data.** It indexes
  generated TypeScript files with fake embeddings and an in-memory store, so it
  reports batching and bookkeeping without a provider account or network calls.

**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Changed
- **The dev toolchain moves to OpenCode 2.4.1.** `@opencode/plugin` and
  `@opencode/theme` are pinned to exactly 2.4.1 in devDependencies, and
  `@opentui/core` and `@opentui/solid` to exactly 0.9.4. The OpenTUI pin is not
  cosmetic: `@opencode/theme` 2.4.1 pins its `@opentui/core` peer to exactly
  0.9.4, so the caret this repository used before would resolve a newer OpenTUI
  and leave npm reporting an invalid peer. The consumer peers do not change:
  `@opencode/plugin >=2.2.7` and `solid-js >=1.9.0`. The Desktop page still uses
  the settings components added in 2.2.6, so the floor stays 2.2.7; the
  devDependencies follow the current host (CLI 2.4.1) so the typecheck sees the
  SDK it ships.
- **The tool wrapper no longer reads `context.signal`.** OpenCode 2.4.1 turned
  it into a getter whose first read opts a call into cooperative stop; a tool
  that never observes it would then be asked to finish instead of being
  interrupted. None of this plugin's tools observes the signal, so leaving it
  unread preserves the previous Stop behaviour. The dependency test now also
  checks the theme's exact `@opentui/core` peer, and the README documents that
  `@latest` plugins update themselves since 2.4.0.

**Install**

```bash
npm install @javierkaiser/opencode-indexing
```

---


### Fixed
- **The re-run guard no longer tells an installed user to delete
  `indexing.json`.** With the plugin installed, the other half of the guard
  would still skip, so that instruction went in circles. The message now points
  at Settings → Indexing, and the README distinguishes an installed plugin from
  a settings file without one: only the latter can be removed and re-run to
  apply the profile.
